samples.question: The picture shows a plain light square sprinkled all over with small grey specks. Every speck is a disc of exactly the same size and exactly the same grey, and no speck touches another, so the specks differ only in where they sit. The specks are not spread evenly: their crowding rises steadily along one straight direction across the picture, so the side of the picture that this direction points to carries the most specks per unit of area and the opposite side carries the fewest. There is no drawn line, no shading, no outline and no change of speck size or colour marking this direction; only the changing crowding shows it. Four coloured discs - red, green, blue and orange - are placed at four different places on one circle centred on the middle of the picture, and all four are the same size. Take the direction that runs from the middle of the picture toward the crowded side of the speck field. Exactly one of the four coloured discs lies closer to that direction, measured as an angle seen from the middle of the picture, than any of the other three. The colours of the discs, which disc sits where on the circle, the number of specks, the size of the specks and the total amount of ink carry no information about the answer. Which coloured disc lies closest in direction to the crowded side of the speck field? Answer red, green, blue or orange.
